properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 4:52PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 452 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Edgewater, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Port Orange, New Smyrna Beach, Edgewater, South Daytona, and Daytona
Beach Shores.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel
clouds. On rare occasions they can briefly touch down, producing wind
gusts over 50 mph. If a funnel cloud is spotted move indoors and
report your sighting to the National Weather Service.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Walton, Bay, Gulf, and Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 12:14PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor has reached Moderate Flood Stage due to
recent northeast winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across
the basin. River levels are forecast to remain just above Moderate
Flood Stage through this weekend and into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM EDT Saturday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady at around 3.2
feet through the weekend.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 11:06AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Cypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.

Anclote River At Elfers at Little Road affecting Pasco County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Cypress Creek and
Anclote River remain elevated. With additional heavy rainfall
forecast, water levels are expected to continue rising, and could
reach minor flood stage in the next few days.

Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and
recent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady
before slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the
river is forecast to remain in flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Cypress Creek at SR 54 Worthington Gardens.

* WHEN...From Monday afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Flooding begins at the recreation area on
State Road 54.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 6.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday afternoon and continue rising to 8.1 feet Tuesday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.1
feet on 05/29/1976.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast and northern Florida, including the
following areas, in northeast Florida, Baker. In northern Florida,
Eastern Hamilton, Gilchrist, Northern Columbia, Southeastern
Columbia, Southwestern Columbia, Suwannee, Union and Western
Hamilton.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A lifting warm front and moisture from the remnants of Tropical
Cyclone Isaias passing northwest of the area will bring rounds of
moderate to heavy showers and thunderstorms across areas of
Southeast Georgia and the Suwannee Valley of Northeast Florida
today. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are likely
with locally higher amounts possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 10 at 12:18AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Indian River, Saint Lucie, Martin,
and Brevard Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
